:JUDGMENT:

This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 19.01.2022 at about 10.30 a.m. she was proceeding as pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg.No. SCCH-5 KA-06-HL-3546 which was ridden by her friend on Nagavalli-Honnudike Road, near Honnudike Temple, Gulur Hobli, Tumkur District, the rider of the said motor cycle was riding the same at high speed in rash and negligent manner without following traffic rules running over the hump, due to the said impact, she fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, she was taken to Government Hospital,
Tumkur, wherein she took treatment as inpatient, for which she has spent an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- towards medial and other expenses.

3. At the time of the accident she was aged about 29 years, hale and healthy, working as coolie,
thereby earning Rs.15,000/- p.m., due to this accident she is not able to work as she was doing prior to the accident, she has lost her earnings.

Out of this accident crime SCCH-5 No.38/2022 is registered against the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-HL-3546 before the Hebbur Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC, R/w. Sec.187 of MV Act.
R1 is the owner, R2 is insurer of the said motor cycle, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% p.a.
4.
On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.

Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and admitted issuance of insurance policy to the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-HL-3546 and its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

Further he seeks protection under Sec.147 and 149(2) of M.V.Act,
there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of SCCH-5 M.V.Act.

Further submitted that, the above said motor cycle was not at all involved in the alleged accident and rider of the motor cycle was not having valid and effective driving license to ride the motor cycle as on the date of accident.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:

sentences.text:
Whether Petitioner proves that, on 19.01.2022 at about 10.30 a.m. when the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on a motor cycle near Nagavalli-Honnudike Road, near Honnudike Temple, Gulur Hobli, Tumakur District,
at that time, rider of the same motor cycle bearing Reg.No. KA-06-HL-3546 ride at a verh high speed in a rash and negligent SCCH-5 manner and run the motor cycle over the hump, due to which, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition? If so,
from which respondent?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove her case, Petitioner herself deposed her evidence as PW-1 and marked 9 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9 and closed her evidence.
On the other hand, Legal Manager of respondent No.2 is examined as RW-1 and marked 1 document as per Ex.R.1 and closed his evidence.

7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
SCCH-5 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:- In order to prove her case, petitioner has deposed her evidence as PW-1, in her chief-examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in her petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of seizure mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.7.
SCCH-5 9.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and records those have marked i.e., as FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, seizure mahazar, IMV Report and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 19.01.2022 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
10.

Per contra, except oral evidence of RW-1 and filing of written statement, respondent No.2 has not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.
Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of Jyothi.

the accident held on 19.01.2022 at about 10.30 a.m. while she was proceeding as pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg.No. KA-06-HL-3546 SCCH-5 which was ridden by her friend on Nagavalli-Honnudike Road, near Honnudike Temple, Gulur Hobli, Tumkur District.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
11. On the other hand, the Legal Manager of respondent No.2 is examined as RW-1 and exhibited copy of policy as Ex.R.1.
The police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the rider of the motor cycle.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in her favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

12. Issue No.2:- As per the case of the petitioner, she was aged about 29 years, for proof of her age,
she SCCH-5 has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.9, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner is 09.02.1993 and the alleged accident is occurred on 19.01.2022,
accordingly relying on Ex.P.9 her age is considered about 29 years as on the date of accident.

Further she was working as Coolie and thereby earning Rs.15,000/- p.m. to prove the said fact,
there are no documents on record.

13. As per the evidence of the petitioner, she had sustained swelling and tenderness over the left forearm, bleeding from nose, swelling and tenderness over dento- alveolar, haematoma over the upper lip, segmental/dentoalvolear fracture with missing of teeth.

In this regard she has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.6 and outpatient record marked as Ex.P.8.
SCCH-5 14.

Further for having incurring of the expenditure i.e., medical charges, petitioner has not placed any bills nor other records like discharge summary, X-ray films, medical bills, medical prescriptions and also not examined the concerned Doctor, but on perusal of the facts, wound certificate and evidence of PW-1 corroborated to believe the injuries sustained by the petitioner out of the accident.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.40,000/-, because petitioner only sustained simple injuries i.e., she has not caused any cut injuries nor fractures not permanent disability.
15. Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.40,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.
SCCH-5 16.

In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.2312910142140700000 which is valid for the period from 03.09.2021 to 02.09.2026, the alleged accident was occurred on 19.01.2022 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.
Further driver of the offending vehicle by name Lakshmana did not possess valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident, accordingly charge sheet is filed against him for Jyothi.

Under such circumstances, naturally R1/owner is liable to pay the compensation in favour of petitioner, but as per the observations made and findings given by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd.
V / s.

Swarna Singh and other reported in AIR 2004 SC 1531 and in case of SCCH-5 Pappu and another V/s. Vinod Kumar Lamba and another reported in AIR 2018 SC 592, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, it is just and necessary to issue directions against R2 Insurance Company to satisfy the petitioner by way of depositing the award amount within 60 days from the date of this order with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and recover from the R1/owner through process of law.

sentences.text: Accordingly, I have answered above Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: : 
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- (Rupees Forty Thousand Only) with SCCH-5 interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order and recover from the respondent No.1 with due process of law.
The Petitioner is entitled to get release entire award amount through e-payment directly to her account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
